song.notes:
The Hymns of Mesomedes Four pieces by (or transmitted with) Mesomedes of Crete, citharode at the court of Hadrian, c. 130 AD, as one song in scenes: Muse, Calliope, Helios, Nemesis. Source: M. L. West, Ancient Greek Music (Oxford 1992), ch. 10, nos. 16-19, pp. 302-8, in his transcription a tone above the manuscripts' pitch; E. Pöhlmann, Denkmäler altgriechischer Musik (DAM), nos. 1, 2, 4, 5. The manuscripts transmit nos. 16-18 as one sequence, two short proems and then the Hymn to the Sun, and no. 19 as its companion piece; all four are in the Lydian notation and are played here in one tuning. The English versions below are ours, not West's; see his pages for his translations.
SCENES Intro (looped) - Muse - Interlude 1 (looped) - Calliope - Interlude 2 (looped) - Helios - Interlude 3 (looped) - Nemesis - Outro. The four named scenes play once; the Intro and the Interludes loop until the operator moves on, and any of them can be skipped. Tempo is quarter = 80 throughout (2 rows per eighth) and broadens only in the Outro (66).
MUSE - Invocation of the Muse. West no. 16, p. 302; DAM 1. E mode. 12/8, one bar a line. Áeide Moûsá moi phílē, / molpês d' emês katárchou; aúrē dè sôn ap' alséōn / emàs phrénas doneítō. "Sing to me, dear Muse, and lead off my song; let a breeze from your groves set my mind stirring." Begins and ends on C (West's e); range B-flat to A-flat. West prints 12/8 with a quadruplet (two quarters in the time of three eighths, here 3 rows each) at the start of lines 2 and 3. Conjecture: the first, second and fourth notes of line 2 (C, F, F on mol-, -pês, -mês) are missing in the manuscripts and supplied by West. Lines 3-4 have West's g-sharp three times (ap' al-, and in the melisma on -mâs): an accidental foreign to the Lydian key whose reading West calls not wholly certain; he follows the usual view, and it is played here as E-up (81/64), outside the scale, as in Calliope bar 4.
CALLIOPE - Invocation of Calliope and Apollo. West no. 17, p. 303; DAM 2. E mode. 2/4. Kalliópeia sophā́, Mousôn prokathāgéti terpnôn, kaì sophè mystodóta, Lātoûs góne, Dḗlie Paiā́n, eumeneîs páresté moi. "Wise Calliope, who lead the delightful Muses, and you, wise giver of the mysteries, Leto's son, Delian Paian: be kind and stand by me." Copied from mesomedes_calliope.xml (melody and second kithara, its rows 16-135), with one correction: bar 10 (-toûs góne) is a c' b in West, F A-flat G, where the earlier file has F G F; West's prose confirms it (the line climbs the scale from c to c'). The earlier file is left as it was. Bar 4 keeps West's g-sharp as E-up (Winnington- Ingram reads g, E-flat). The last line is one 12/8 bar in West; scenes carry one time signature, so it lies across three 2/4 bars here. The second kithara moves to the A-flat-E-flat frame for line 2 (West's "C major") and back.
HELIOS - Hymn to the Sun. West no. 18, pp. 304-6; DAM 4. E mode. 15/8 (West: 8+7 over 8), one bar a line, 19 lines. 1 Chionoblephárou páter Āoûs, 2 rhodóessan hòs ántyga pṓlōn 3 ptānoîs hyp' íchnessi diṓkeis, 4 chryséaisin agallómenos kómais, 5 perì nôton apeíriton ouranoû 6 aktîna polýstrophon amplékōn, 7 aíglās polyderkéa pāgā̀n 8 perì gaîan hápāsan helíssōn; 9 potamoì dè séthen pyròs ambrótou 10 tíktousin epḗraton hāmérān. 11 soì mèn choròs eúdios astérōn 12 kat' Ólympon ánakta choreúei, 13 áneton mélos aièn aeídōn, 14 Phoibēḯdi terpómenos lýrāi, 15 glaukà dè pároithe Selā́nā 16 chrónon hṓrion hāgemoneúei 17 leukôn hypò sýrmasi móschōn; 18 gánytai dé té soi nóos eumenḕs 19 polyeímona kósmon helíssōn. "Father of Dawn with her snow-white eyelids, you who drive your rose-red chariot behind the winged tread of your horses, exulting in your golden hair, plaiting your ever-turning ray across the boundless back of heaven, winding the far-seen spring of your radiance about the whole earth; and rivers of your deathless fire give birth to the lovely day. For you the calm chorus of the stars dances over Olympus its lord, singing for ever its unfettered song, delighting in Phoebus' lyre; and before you the pale Moon leads on the season's time, drawn by white heifers; and your kindly mind is glad as it turns the many-robed world." Begins and ends on C (West's e); range A-flat 3 to A-flat 4, the outer notes only in passing. Lacuna: line 10, the syllable -mé- of hāméran has no note (an eighth rest). Line-end rhythms follow West: where two long syllables close the line he gives a dotted quarter and a quarter, and divided long syllables as printed.
NEMESIS - Hymn to Nemesis. West no. 19, pp. 306-8; DAM 5. G mode on the same notes: the tonic is West's g, E-flat, with A-flat and B-flat as secondary centres; the song's key stays C. 15/8, one bar a line, 20 lines. 1 Némesi pteróessa, bíou rhopā́, 2 kyanôpi theā́, thýgater Díkās, 3 hā̀ koûpha phryágmata thnātôn 4 epécheis adámanti chalīnôi, 5 échthousa d' hýbrin oloā̀n brotôn 6 mélana phthónon ektòs elaúneis. 7 hypò sòn trochòn ástaton astibê 8 charopà merópōn stréphetai týchā, 9 lḗthousa dè pàr póda baíneis, 10 gauroúmenon auchéna klī́neis, 11 hypò pêchyn aeì bíoton metreîs, 12 neúeis d' hypò kólpon ophrỳn aeí, 13 zygòn metà cheîra kratoûsa. 14 hī́lēthi mákaira dikaspóle, 15 Némesi pteróessa, bíou rhopā́. 16 Némesin theòn āídomen aphthítān, 17 Nī́kēn tanysípteron obrímān 18 nēmertéa kaì páredron Díkās, 19 hā̀ tā̀n megalānoríān brotôn 20 nemesôsa phéreis katà Tartárou. "Nemesis, winged tilter of the scale of life, dark-eyed goddess, daughter of Justice, you who rein in the empty snortings of mortals with a bridle of adamant and, hating men's ruinous pride, drive black envy out: beneath your wheel, never still and leaving no track, the bright fortune of men turns. Unnoticed you walk at their heel; you bow the neck that is held too high; under your forearm you always measure out life, and always you bend your brow toward your breast, the balance held in your hand. Be gracious, blessed giver of justice, Nemesis, winged tilter of the scale of life. We sing Nemesis, the imperishable goddess, mighty Victory of the spreading wings, the unerring one who sits beside Justice: you who resent the overweening of mortals and bear it down to Tartarus." Begins on F (West's a, leading to the tonic); range A-flat 3 to B-flat 4. Lacunae (rests; the second kithara keeps the frame through them): line 6, the last five syllables (ek-tòs e-laú-neis); line 7, -chòn; line 8, -ró- and -phe-; line 20, everything after the first note (G on ne-). Conjecture: the final E-flat on -rou is not in the manuscript; West's diagram of line-ends (Ex. 10.2) gives g there with a question mark, and it is supplied so that the hymn closes on its tonic. Our padding: West prints line 13 as 13 eighths and line 14 as 14 (a single short first syllable, a short last syllable); an eighth rest before and after line 13 and after line 14 keeps the 15/8 bars aligned.
REALISATION The manuscripts give pitch and rhythm. Ours are the tempo, the instruments, the anabolai, intro, interludes and outro. This is Apollo's music, sung by a citharode to his own kithara: no aulos, no percussion. Without a singer the first kithara carries the sung line, long notes struck harder than short; the second kithara (detuned 4) does what the citharode's left hand did: the frame, tonic and fifth of the current centre (C-G; E-flat-B-flat for Nemesis), struck at each line's start and again at the caesura, with a short plectrum run into each line. Each scene opens with a one-bar anabole; the Intro is the old two-bar run up the seven strings, made loopable; each Interlude is one bar of the C-G frame held; the Outro runs down the strings to the E-flat-B-flat frame while the first kithara echoes the rhopā́ cadence.
The scale is nīd qablim, the Phrygian mode on C of the Pythagorean gamut: C D-flat E-flat F G A-flat B-flat = 1/1 256/243 32/27 4/3 3/2 128/81 16/9, West's e f g a b c' d' (his c d below are A-flat B-flat). In 53-EDO's notation the gamut spells these C-sharp-up, E-flat-down, A-flat-down and B-flat-down.
